parsed.why: Most-protective local regime: shield laws, gender-neutral bathrooms, anti-discrimination/hate-crime, repealed policing tool. Still bounded by national passport, visa, federal facilities/custody constraints, so Elevated Risk.

State protections and no facility ban help visitors, but no shield law, hate-crime enforcement unproven, and university capitulation on sports signals pressure; national border/documents remain dominant.

No state gender-identity recourse for visitors, hate-crime gap, appointed boards and a school bathroom policy show hostility; no adult facility ban, but outside four cities discrimination is largely unremedied.

Strong nondiscrimination, shield laws and gender-neutral single-user bathrooms protect visitors; no state facility ban. Caveat about national attacks matters, but local regime is materially safer than average.

State law imposes birth-sex facility exclusion, sports/care bans, no protections or hate-crime statute, invasive documents; universal visitor exposure adds to national passport/federal hostility. Do Not Travel.
